summary.headline: Surya Roshni Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR2,046 crore and PAT 77% to INR60 crore, but steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,006 sits well below the FY27 INR4,600-4,700 guidance.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR2,046 crore (up 28% YoY), EBITDA of INR120 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 77%) were driven mainly by Steel Pipes & Strips, where volume hit a record Q1 of 2.28 lakh tons. Management attributed the EBITDA/ton shortfall to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM cost increases (about INR200/ton), and expects recovery as new orders are booked at higher freight rates. Lighting & Consumer Durables grew 15% to INR456 crore with margin up to 7.9%. The company remains debt-free with net cash of about INR155 crore; buyback and demerger decisions were deferred with no firm timeline.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +17% YoY (from INR31 crore); PBT +12% YoY (from INR21 crore)

financial_highlights.value: About INR155 crore (B.B. Singal cited INR154 crore) as of 30 June 2026

segments.name: Steel Pipes & Strips
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,590 crore (+32% YoY) on record Q1 volume of 2.28 lakh tons (+21% YoY); section, ERW API, spiral, cold rolling and GP pipes led, galvanized soft on delayed government fund releases. Capacity utilisation about 82%, value-added products 47% of volume, exports 20% of segment volume.

segments.name: Lighting & Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR456 crore (+15% YoY), best-ever Q1, led by LED bulbs, battens and downlighters; EBITDA INR36 crore with margin 7.9%, passing through about 7% input cost increase. Professional lighting order book about INR150 crore.

segments.name: Wire & Cables
segments.commentary: Management said Q1 sales nearly matched FY26 full-year volume; FY26 revenue target INR250 crore, against a 3-year INR500 crore goal. Electrician loyalty program enrolments reached 36,000.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume about 11 lakh tons (+20-22% volume growth); quarterly path of about 2.6-2.65 lakh tons in Q2, 2.8-2.9 lakh in Q3 and about 3.2 lakh in Q4.
FY27 steel EBITDA/ton guidance of INR4,600-4,700 reiterated; management expects about INR4,400-4,500 in Q2 and INR4,600-4,700 full year, implying above INR5,000 in H2 per Q1 analyst math.
Company FY27 EBITDA guided at INR670-680 crore on revenue of INR9,400-9,500 crore; Q2 EBITDA about INR150 crore and H2 about INR400 crore.
Lighting FY27: revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore FY26), value growth 19-22%, volume growth about 25%, EBITDA about INR200 crore.

Steel value growth 30%+ expected for FY27; US market contribution 10-11% of volume (about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27), total exports about 3 lakh tons; export share of steel to rise from about 20% to 25%.
Ocean freight: new orders booked at higher rates, with July impact described as very low and no freight impact expected in the next two months; break-bulk shipping arranged for US volumes.
Full-year API/spiral EBITDA/ton expected to recover from Q1 INR3,420 to about INR5,000 (vs INR5,500-5,700 in FY26).
Per-ton cost reduction target of about INR1,100 and manpower cost reduction of about 20% over the next year; 15-18% CAGR targeted for the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capacity 14 lakh tons currently; target 16 lakh tons by end-FY27 with three DFT mills commissioning between August and December 2026 at Gujarat, Malanpur and Bahadurgarh; about 2 million tons by FY28-29.
Adding 2-3 lakh tons of capacity every year; capex about INR100 crore for the 14-to-16 lakh ton expansion, funded from internal accruals.

Hindupur (South) greenfield-style expansion on 10 additional acres: first mill about January 2027, total 4-mill plant adding about 15,000 tons initially, about INR60 crore investment, roughly 3 lakh tons overall.
Greenfield projects under evaluation with clarity promised by next board meeting; expansions focus on DFT and section pipes.
demand_pricing: Steel order book INR800 crore (export API orders include 78,000 tons for the US) vs INR1,000 crore at end-March; management said about 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed.
Ocean freight rose sharply; Q1 exports carried about INR3,800/ton higher freight, costing about INR800/ton of blended EBITDA. Management says new orders are priced at the higher freight.

US market opened for ERW API pipes, with realisation EBITDA/ton of about INR7,200 in Q1; Middle East orders fell (roughly one-third of usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter now able to ship), and API orders down about 50%.
Steel prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April, then fell in May-June, leaving the quarter roughly neutral on inventory; steel now seen stable within INR1,000/ton.
Q1 API/spiral EBITDA/ton of INR3,420 cited with coating material as a significant drag; water pipe faces higher competition.
Lighting: about 80% of production in-house, about 20% outsourced, with the outsourced share largely made exclusively for Surya.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta (Enigma): how will steel EBITDA/ton reach INR4,700-4,800 when Q1 was about INR4,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 volume was about 2.30 lakh tons vs 2.65 lakh planned (port delays, Middle East orders down 8,000-10,000 tons, API/spiral shortfall of 8,000-10,000 tons). Margin gap of about INR700/ton was attributed to ocean freight (about INR800/ton on total volume) and coating, gas and ORM costs (about INR200/ton). New orders are priced at higher freight, and Q2 is guided at INR4,400-4,500/ton with full year INR4,600-4,700.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta: how much inventory loss occurred in Q1 given steel price swings?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose INR3,000-4,000/ton in April and fell in May-June, so the quarter was roughly neutral with no inventory impact. Steel is now seen stable within INR1,000/ton. About 25,000 tons of imported material already at port should support Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Kiran (TableTree): why did the steel order book fall from INR1,000 crore to INR800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier book was cleared and fresh orders carry higher freight; Middle East shipments are about one-third of the usual 15,000-20,000 tons per quarter, and API orders are down about 50%. About 75-80% of business is distribution-type and fixed, so the drop has limited volume impact.

qa_highlights.question: Kiran: is the US export product GI or API/spiral, and what is the FY27 and FY28 export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The US product is ERW API pipe, with Q1 realisation around INR7,200/ton, helped by freight; break-bulk tie-ups should lower freight exposure. US share of steel is seen at 8-10% (later 10-11%, about 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27); export share rises from about 20% to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Love Gupta (Counter Cyclical): any update on buyback and demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback work is ongoing and a decision is expected 'very soon', with no material to disclose yet; working capital rose during steel price swings. Demerger is a matter of board consensus, with the MD saying the timing is right once macro improves.

qa_highlights.question: Pranav (Rare Enterprises): why delay demerger or buyback, and will pricing offset the freight-driven EBITDA erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD cited standalone strength of both businesses and geopolitical uncertainty, and said he sees no logic against demerger. On pricing, freight impact on past orders will not recur in coming quarters, and US volume is expected at 1.2-1.25 lakh tons in FY27, with total exports about 3 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Shantanu Basu (SMIFS): what drove the drop in API/spiral EBITDA/ton, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 API/spiral EBITDA/ton was INR3,420, hit by coating material costs and lower-margin water pipe mix with higher competition. Management expects recovery to about INR5,000 for FY27 vs INR5,500-5,700 in FY26; Middle East freight moves are outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Resham Jain (VVD): API tender outlook, capacity locations, and whether FY27 EBITDA guidance holds?
qa_highlights.answer: API tenders are rising and the company is bidding, though conversion takes time. Capacity goes from 14 to 16 lakh tons by end-FY27; Hindupur adds a 4-mill plant with first mill around January 2027, about INR60 crore investment, roughly 3 lakh tons overall. FY27 EBITDA guided at INR670-680 crore: Q2 about INR150 crore, H2 about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta: is Q2 EBITDA INR150 crore, is July freight hit ongoing, and what Q2 volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed Q2 EBITDA about INR150 crore. Freight impact in July is very low and should be absent in the next two months. Q2 volume guided at 2.6 to 2.65 lakh tons minimum.

qa_highlights.question: Raj Mehta: why is margin under pressure QoQ, how does the company compare with peers, and what is the 5-year vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 volume growth of 21% and value growth of 32% versus peers (APL Apollo 8%, Jindal SAW 13%, Ratnamani -16%). Lighting value growth guided at 19-20% and steel volume 20-22% with value 30%+. Next 5 years: 15-18% CAGR targeted, manpower cost cut about 20% in one year, and greenfield projects to be clarified by next board meeting.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: capex for 14 to 16 lakh tons, FY27 lighting vs steel mix, and lighting outsourcing share?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR100 crore from internal accruals. Lighting FY27 revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore) with EBITDA about INR200 crore; company FY27 revenue INR9,400-9,500 crore, EBITDA INR670-680 crore. About 20% of lighting is outsourced and 80% in-house; outsourced output is largely made exclusively for Surya.

risks_watch: Full-year steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,600-4,700 needs about INR5,000+ in H2 after Q1 of INR4,006; freight and coating cost recovery is management's key assumption.
Steel order book fell to INR800 crore from INR1,000 crore at end-March; Middle East shipments run at about one-third of normal and API orders are down about 50%.
Volume shortfall carried into Q2: about 8,000-10,000 tons of spillover at port, with Q2 guided at 2.6-2.65 lakh tons against 2.3 lakh in Q1.
Buyback and demerger decisions remain open with no firm timeline; working capital rose during steel price swings.
Execution of 14-to-16 lakh ton DFT mill commissioning (Aug-Dec 2026) and Hindupur first mill (January 2027); greenfield clarity promised at next board meeting.
Galvanized pipe demand soft due to delayed government fund releases; water pipe faces higher competition.
key_quotes: And we are fully committed that full year of FY27 guidance of INR4,600 to INR4,700 per ton EBITDA will be achieved.
So, we are expecting around INR 150 crore in Q2. And our target is INR 400 crore for the rest H2.
Now, almost all the orders currently in hand or coming in are being booked at the new increased freight rates.
But very soon, we will do some corporate action and inform you quickly.
I also believe there is no logic in not doing the demerger. I strongly believe.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year guidance and volume growth, repeatedly reiterating the INR4,600-4,700 EBITDA/ton and INR670-680 crore EBITDA targets despite a Q1 miss. Becomes noticeably evasive on buyback and demerger timing (no firm decision, "very soon" language) and on steel price direction, which it said is outside its control.
